ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a rectangular wire frame MNPQ in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface outward, with magnetic induction intensity magnitude B, rotates with constant angular velocity ω around the diagonal line NQ. It is known that the length of MN is $l_{1}$, the length of NP is $l_{2}$, and the resistance of the wire frame is R. At time t＝0 the plane of the wire frame coincides with the paper surface. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question 1
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, a rectangular wire frame MNPQ in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface outward, with magnetic induction intensity magnitude B, rotates with constant angular velocity \(\omega\) around the diagonal line NQ. It is known that the length of MN is \(l_{1}\), the length of NP is \(l_{2}\), and the resistance of the wire frame is R. At time \(t=0\), the plane of the wire frame coincides with the paper surface. What is the effective value of the induced electromotive force produced by the rectangular wire frame?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a rectangular wire frame MNPQ in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface outward, with magnetic induction intensity magnitude B, rotates with constant angular velocity \(\omega\) around the diagonal line NQ. It is known that the length of MN is \(l_{1}\), the length of NP is \(l_{2}\), and the resistance of the wire frame is R. At time \(t=0\), the plane of the wire frame coincides with the paper surface. What is the effective value of the induced electromotive force produced by the rectangular wire frame?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is the rectangular wire frame MNPQ, M and N are on the left side, Q and P are on the right side, the dashed line connects from N to Q, indicating that the wire frame rotates around the diagonal line NQ; the black dots uniformly distributed in the background indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward. The problem statement gives that the length of MN is l1 and the length of NP is l2, so the area of the wire frame is S = l1 l2. Reasoning: At t = 0, the plane of the wire frame coincides with the paper surface, and the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward, therefore at this time the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the wire frame, and the magnetic flux is maximum. The wire frame rotates uniformly with angular velocity ω around the diagonal line NQ located in the plane of the wire frame. After time t has passed, the normal of the wire frame has rotated by angle ωt relative to the direction of the magnetic field, therefore the magnetic flux is Φ(t) = B S cos(ωt) = B l1 l2 cos(ωt). By Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of the induced electromotive force as a function of time is ε(t) = |−dΦ/dt| = B l1 l2 ω |sin(ωt)|, and the peak value of its sinusoidal alternating electromotive force is εm = B l1 l2 ω. The effective value of a sinusoidal quantity is equal to the peak value divided by √2, so εrms = εm/√2 = B l1 l2 ω/√2 = (√2/2) B l1 l2 ω.
